questiontext.text:
Goal

A packhouse prepares harvested fruit for shipping. Its weighbridge weighs each bin and adds its mass to one running total. At Riwaka, several pickers can place bins on the scale at the same time. No bin may disappear from the total.

Read
  • sync.Mutex. Read the complete type documentation. What state does a zero-value Mutex have? What must never happen to a Mutex after first use?
  • Mutex.Lock. What happens if a goroutine calls Lock while another goroutine holds the lock?
  • Mutex.Unlock. Read all four sentences. Which Unlock call causes a run-time error? Must the unlocking goroutine also have locked it?
Required: sync.Mutex
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Adding to a total is three steps, read the old number, add the bin, then write the new number. When two goroutines run those steps at once, both read the same old number and one bin goes missing.
  • A lock lets one goroutine at a time into the lines that touch the total and makes the others wait. Both Add and Total need the lock. The Mutex page names the two methods that take the lock and give it back.

testcode.text: var s Scale fmt.Println(s.Total()) s.Add(7) s.Add(3) fmt.Println(s.Total())

questiontext.text:
Goal

A sailing clearance tells a skipper whether a boat may still leave port. The Port Taranaki harbourmaster can recall it at any time, and it expires automatically when its curfew passes.

Read
  • context. Read the Context interface and its Err documentation. When does Err return nil? Which two named errors can it return? Can a later call to Err return a different error?
  • context.WithDeadline. Read the complete documentation. What does each return value do? What should you do with the second return value? What is the type of the second parameter? Which function on that type gives the current time?
  • context.CancelFunc. Read all four lines. What does calling a CancelFunc do? What happens on the second call?
Required: context.WithDeadline
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • A context tree starts at a root that nothing cancels. Find the function that returns such a root. Where does its documentation say the root belongs?
  • Two of the constructors on that page return a pair, the new context and a function that ends it. One of the two takes a moment in time, and nothing in the doc says that moment must be in the future. To tell the two endings apart, use errors.Is against the package's two named error values.

testcode.text: ctx, cancel := harbour() fmt.Println(clearance(ctx)) cancel() fmt.Println(clearance(ctx))
ctx, cancel := curfew() defer cancel() fmt.Println(clearance(ctx))
ctx, cancel := curfew() fmt.Println(clearance(ctx)) cancel() fmt.Println(clearance(ctx))
one, cancelOne := harbour() two, cancelTwo := harbour() defer cancelTwo() cancelOne() cancelOne() fmt.Println(clearance(one), clearance(two))

questiontext.text:
Goal

A depot dispatches one driver and sends each new stop over the radio. When the shift ends, the driver must return and no depot worker may remain waiting to send another stop. When the radio closes, rounds returns the stops reached in radio order and a nil error. When the shift ends first, rounds returns the stops reached so far and the context's own error, unchanged. dispatch passes back whatever rounds returned. If the shift is already over when the driver sets off, rounds returns at once and takes nothing off the radio.

Read
  • Go Concurrency Patterns: Context. Read Context and Derived contexts. Which method returns a channel? What happens to that channel? Which function returns a pair whose second value stops the work?
  • context.Context. Read the full Err documentation. What does Err return before the channel closes? Can Err return a different value after closure?
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • A select with two receive cases waits until one of them can go ahead, then takes that one. Put the radio on one case and the context's channel on the other, so the driver stops waiting when the shift ends. Ask the context outright before the loop as well, because a shift can be over before the driver sets off.
  • A send on a channel with no capacity waits for a receiver, so the goroutine calling the stops has to watch the context too. A goroutine that ignores the context waits for ever when the round is cut short, and dispatch can never wait for it.

testcode.text: ctx, cancel := shift() defer cancel() got, err := dispatch(ctx, []string{"wharf", "yard", "gate"}) fmt.Printf("%q %v\n", got, err == nil)
ctx, cancel := shift() defer cancel() radio := make(chan string) go func() { radio <- "wharf" close(radio) }() got, err := rounds(ctx, radio) fmt.Printf("%q %v\n", got, err == nil)
ctx, cancel := shift() radio := make(chan string) go func() { radio <- "wharf" radio <- "yard" cancel() }() got, err := rounds(ctx, radio) fmt.Printf("%q %v\n", got, err)

ctx, cancel := shift() cancel() early := 0 var earlyErr error for range 200 { waiting := make(chan string, 1) waiting <- "wharf" got, err := rounds(ctx, waiting) early += len(got) earlyErr = err } late := 0 var lateErr error for range 200 { got, err := dispatch(ctx, []string{"wharf", "yard"}) late += len(got) lateErr = err } fmt.Println(early, earlyErr) fmt.Println(late, lateErr)
